usableMeans.definition: The tab reaches a working state without reloading or signing in again, with its expected data available and actions working. Not every initial request has to succeed. A rendered shell with missing data is not usable.
usableMeans.expectedData: On /dashboard: the "Dashboard" heading is rendered, no "Could not load:" warning is shown, and no data request the tab made (by method, path and query) is left failed, the regional-settings request excepted (see shell).
usableMeans.shell: The shell is part of the expected data. Company data: the latest GET /api/settings/company of the tab is 2xx and the sidebar shows the server's company name. Regional settings: judged by effect, not by the request: the formats the tab applies (localStorage, which the application fills from the answer and every formatter reads) equal the server's; a tab whose own request was refused is counted separately.
usableMeans.user: A non-administrator. Recovery through a page only an administrator can open does not count: such a step is refused and fails the tab.
usableMeans.recovery: Only through the sidebar links the user's role is shown (read from frontend/src/config/navigation.tsx), never a reload, a URL load or a sign-in: Sales > Sales Orders, then Dashboard. At most 3 actions per tab, paced so that api_limit (20r/s, burst 40) has room for a page of requests. When only shell data is missing, one round trip is made and then no more: no page change asks for it again.
usableMeans.automaticRetry: The application itself repeats GET /api/settings/company after a 429 (and no other request). That is not a recovery action; per tab it is recorded whether the company data came on the first request or by that retry, how long the retry took, and whether the retries were used up.
usableMeans.action: Sidebar: Sales > Customers. A fresh request for the list answered 2xx and its rows on screen; at most 3 tries.
usableMeans.notJudged: The status indicator's polls of /api/health (every 30 s, self-repairing); 429s among them are counted per tab.

rounds.description: one tab signs out while the others are still loading

signOutAttempt.why: the attempt behaved and overlapped no delayed request; set up again

judgement.scope: W1 shows that the tabs of a restored window coordinate their refresh, that a restored window puts little load on session_limit, and that at 5, 10, 20 tabs every tab reaches its expected data without the user acting. How long that takes is reported and does not block. It does not measure the capacity of that zone, which is never approached, and it does not establish how many tabs a restored window can hold: that is bounded by the general api_limit (issue #1353).

howEachRoundReachesTheSessionZone.a: Current tokens: there is nothing to refresh, and the application sends no /auth/me on load. The round normally sends nothing to the zone.
howEachRoundReachesTheSessionZone.b: Every tab starts with an expired access token: one tab takes the lease and refreshes, the others adopt its tokens.
howEachRoundReachesTheSessionZone.c: As (b), plus the explicit logout of the tab that signs out.

judgement.blocking: At N = 5, 10, 20: no 429 on refresh, logout or me in rounds (a), (b) and (c); in (a) and (b) every tab usable, no in-app recovery action; in (a) the access token current and in (b) expired when the tabs opened; in (c) the logout sent and answered 2xx and every tab on the login page without a reload. Not blocking: 429s on business endpoints, counted at every size; the completion time, reported against 5 s, 10 s and 15 s (#1359).

M1.what: one raw read, one tab idle

M2.what: one raw read in four tabs at once while a fifth writes

diagnostic.statement: M3 and M4 are diagnostic: measured and recorded with their environment, with no threshold and no pass or fail. M5 is diagnostic as before.

criteria.preserved: The hard gate and its transaction-completion semantics are unchanged. None of the simulated optimizations was implemented, and no read is resolved before its transaction completes.

formerProvisionalTargets.statement: The earlier M3 and M4 targets (p95 at most 10 ms in one tab, 20 ms in four) were provisional. They were replaced by the criteria above; they were NOT met, and a run that passes today has not met them either.

runInWhichTheyFailed.outcome: M1 and M2 passed. M3 (99 / 330.1 ms) and M4 (205.3 / 603.3 ms), one tab / four tabs, failed the 10 / 20 ms targets, and the run exited with status 1.

latency.rule: M1 and M2 block, each on the median p95 of 3 repetitions. M3, M4 and M5 are diagnostic and are not judged. Maxima and p99 are recorded and never block.

competingWorkload.capturedBy: run.sh, on the host, just before measure.mjs: docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}'
competingWorkload.note: No container was restarting on the host when the list was taken.

M1.what: one raw read, one tab idle; 500 sequential read-only transactions per repetition

M2.what: one raw read in four tabs at once (500 each per repetition) while a fifth tab commits a write every 100 ms

M3.what: the adapter's own `read` timings while the dashboard, the products list and a sales order load
M3.status: M3 and M4 are diagnostic: measured and recorded with their environment, with no threshold and no pass or fail. M5 is diagnostic as before.

M4.what: per request, gate-before + gate-after: wall time added to that request, queueing included
M4.status: M3 and M4 are diagnostic: measured and recorded with their environment, with no threshold and no pass or fail. M5 is diagnostic as before.

M5.label: Aggregate-cost estimate. Diagnostic only: no threshold, and no share of page load is computed from it.
M5.note: Requests on a page overlap, so the sum of their gate waits is not the time the gate adds to the page load; it is an upper bound on it.
M5.what: median of 5 loads per page: navigation to last API response delivered, number of requests, and the SUM of all gate waits
